title: Nobel Peace Prize awarded to Navi Pillay of International Court of Justice

blocks.text: Navanethem (Navi) Pillay of South Africa, a former United Nations high commissioner for human rights and judge on the International Court of Justice, was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in Oslo on Friday.
Past winners include Nelson Mandela, Martin Luther King, Malala Yousafzai
2026 Nobel Peace Prize awarded to Navi Pillay

The committee called Pillay, 85, "one of the great defenders of international legal principles in our time" and said "her commitment to justice and human dignity is a source of hope and inspiration to all those who seek to bring about a more peaceful world."

"A common thread ​runs from her early work defending Nelson Mandela and ​others who stood up against ⁠apartheid to ⁠her ‌service as a judge in some of the key international court cases of our time," the committee ⁠said.
Pillay's honour, the committee said, comes at a time of "existential challenges" for international law.
"We see a shift towards power politics at the expense of legal frameworks and global respect for law and justice," said Jørgen Watne Frydnes, chair of the Norwegian Nobel Committee.
The peace prize is the fifth Nobel awarded this week, after literature, ‌chemistry, physics and medicine. Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado won in 2025.

The Nobel Peace ​Prize, worth 12 million Swedish crowns, ⁠or about $1.7 million Cdn, is due to be ⁠presented in Oslo on Dec. 10, ⁠the ⁠anniversary ​of the death of Swedish industrialist Alfred Nobel, ​who ⁠founded the awards in his 1895 will.
